Guidance & outlook: As of the end of Q1 FY27, our cumulative tr ee plantation has crossed 6.3 million trees with nearly 80,000 samplings planted during the quarter to strengthen green belt coverage and enhance local biodiversity around our operations.
Inflation is expected to rise 5% in FY27 from 2.1% in FY26.
The market is expected to have a deficit of 1 million tons in calendar year '26 compared to pre-conflict expectations of about 0.3 million tons.
Growth & demand: On the demand side, China continues to see healthy growth with consumption up 2% to around 12 million tons, driven by strong demand from new energy vehicles and robust exports of semi- fabricated and finished products.
Outside China, demand declined by around 2% as softer conditions in Europe, North America and Middle East more than offset growth in India.
We estimate aluminum demand in quarter 1 of FY27 at around 1.5 million tons representing growth of approximately 3% year-on-year.
Margins & costs: Global inflation is projected to rise from 4.1% in 2025 to 4.7% in 2026, reflecting higher energy, food and fertilizer prices and signaling a temporary pause in the global disinflation process.
EBITDA margins were at a record 55% and continue to be amongst the best in the global industry.
Our quarterly copper EBITDA stood at a record INR918 crores, up 36% year-on-year. on account of better realizations in byproducts and operational efficiencies.
Capex & expansion: We remain on track to add another 414 megawatts of solar and wind capacity as well as 90 megawatts of RE RTC pump storage capacity during the year.
With these additions, our renewable portfolio is expected to reach 884 megawatts of solar wind hydel capacity, along with 125 megawatts of RE RTC capacity by the end of FY27.

Looking at the global aluminum market in quarter 1 of calendar year '26 Chinese aluminum production grew about 3% year-on-year to nearly 11 million tons supported by capacity additions in regions such as Yu nnan and inner Mongolia.
Balance sheet & cash: As of June 2026, our consolidated net debt-to-EBITDA stood at 1.95x below our stated threshold of 2x.
We remain disciplined in our capital allocation approach and committed to maintain net leverage at around 2x on a consol basis.

As we heard from the Novelis call of their expectations of leverage come down below 4x at the consol Hindalco level, should we expect the net debt to be steady at these levels as of March and come down because the underlying cash flows are very, very strong.
Risks & challenges: China is expected to slow from 5% to 4.6% as higher energy prices, persistent uncertainty and structural headwinds weigh on activity.
However, downside risk persists particularly from geopolitical uncertainties, volatility in global financial markets, external headwinds and weather-related disruptions.

Outside China, production declined by around 8% to 7 million tons largely due to disruptions related to the Middle East conflict and the closure of Mozal, although higher output from Indonesia and Europe provided some support.
